title: Compress photos online without uploading to a server
description: Compress images locally in the browser: JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC. Files stay off the cloud — no sign-up, batch and ZIP.
lead: Shrink JPG, PNG, and WebP — or work with PDFs — right in the browser. Files stay on your device: no sign-up, no cloud.
body: PixLocal compresses images on your computer or phone. Handy for websites, marketplaces, email, and messengers: a smaller file means faster uploads.

Unlike many online tools, we never accept your photos on a server. It works like editing a shot in your phone gallery or in Paint: the whole process stays inside your browser. You can batch files and download a ZIP.
By default the long edge is capped at 2560 px — so iPhone photos actually get smaller. Quality, side limit, and KB target can be changed manually.

faq.q: Does my photo really not go over the network during compression?
faq.a: The file contents — yes, they stay put: compression runs on your device, like editing in your gallery or Paint. Opening the site still downloads the page as usual. In DevTools → Network during processing, you will not see your image body uploaded to our server.

faq.q: How is this different from TinyPNG and iLoveIMG?
faq.a: Typical online compressors upload photos to their servers. PixLocal processes the file only in your browser — contents never go to a server or the cloud. There is no cloud lossless like TinyPNG: for icons, CLI optimizers are stronger.
JPG/JPEG, PNG, WebP, and HEIC/HEIF (via a local heic-to/libheif decoder). You can save the result as JPG, WebP, or PNG.

faq.q: Why can HEIC become larger after converting to JPG?
faq.a: HEIC is usually more compact than JPEG. We automatically lower quality and resolution so the JPG becomes lighter than the original. If needed, reduce Max side or quality manually.

faq.q: How do I save to Photos on iPhone?
faq.a: Tap Share and choose Save Image in the system menu. On iOS, Download usually puts the file in Files.

faq.q: What do you use to compress, and is it legal?
faq.a: JPG/PNG/WebP — the browser’s built-in Canvas; HEIC — open-source heic-to (libheif, LGPL-3.0); ZIP — jszip (MIT). Details are in the licenses section on GitHub / LICENSES.md.
No. Open the page, drop files, then download or share the result.

faq.q: Why are all PixLocal tools safe?
faq.a: We use your browser instead of remote servers. Photo and PDF tools run on your device’s CPU. We physically cannot receive your files.

faq.q: Can I use PixLocal without internet?
faq.a: Yes — press Offline in the header and wait for the checklist. Only the current language is saved; your files still never upload.

dualPitch: PixLocal is two toolsets in one place: photo compress & convert, and PDF utilities — both private, both on-device.
